newsitem.title: GREECE: BP-Greece audited but tight-lipped on outcome.
newsitem.headline: BP-Greece audited but tight-lipped on outcome.

text.p: British Petroleum-Greece said it was audited by a finance ministry team for fiscal years 1991-93 but would not comment on media reports it could pay 7.5 billion drachmas ($31.28 million) to settle allegations of tax evasion.

"We believed then and believe now the finding was inaccurate and was based on wrong judgements. Since December 1995, BP Greece has supported its case with indisputable facts before the pertinent committee at the finance ministry," a statement said.

"We have not yet received the committee's final ruling and therefore we cannot and should not comment on various scenarios as to its content. We are certain we have the facts to support our position which is fully legal," BP said.

Media reports said the finance ministry issued a finding in July 1995 and further discussions had been underway with BP. The reports said tax authorities believed they had found extensive concealing of taxable income.
According to financial daily Imerisia the finance ministry's audit department manager George Manousakis was called to testify in the case three days ago.
It said the 7.5 billion drachmas was a settlement proposed by British Petroleum. The investigation was completed in early September and the file had been sent to the public prosecutor's office.
BP executives and Manousakis were unavailable for comment.
British Petroleum said in its statement that BP had operated in Greece since 1951 and in the last 45 years had respected all laws and lived up to its obligations to the Greek state.

British Petroleum is one of the major players in Greece's fuels market along with Texaco, Mobil Shell and Eko. Together they hold a 71.5 percent market share. BP has 17 percent of the gasoline market in Greece.
